clue.text: Airs and graces displayed by no Serb organisation

indicators.note: organising things means putting them into a new order, so the letters before it are rearranged

parts.note: all eight letters of these three words, taken as written

explanation.surface: A Serbian body is praised for having no pretensions or showy manners.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' looks like a link word but its letters belong in the mix with 'no Serb'.
explanation.definitionFit: Snobbery is the condescending attitude that shows itself in putting on affected manners and superior behaviour.

clue.text: Downhill race's small detour over nothing …

definitions.text: Downhill race's small detour over nothing

parts.words: Downhill race's small detour over nothing
parts.note: surface reading: a skier takes a little detour on a downhill course
setter's reading: a ski race made of repeated small swerves round gates, over snowy ground with nothing in the way

explanation.surface: A downhill skier briefly swings off line, and the ellipsis carries the thought into the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: No clean letter-by-letter wordplay emerges (S for small fits, the rest does not), so this is best read as a description of the race itself: a zigzag of small detours round the gates.
explanation.definitionFit: This alpine ski event has competitors weaving between poles, so the course is a chain of short deviations from a straight line.

clue.text: … as couple playing zoom in for this

definitions.note: a phrase describing what the camera achieves rather than a synonym

indicators.note: playing about with something puts it in a fresh arrangement, so the letters are shuffled

parts.note: the eight letters of these two words

explanation.surface: A photographer watches a pair at play and moves the lens in tight.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis only joins the surfaces of 2 and 3 down; each clue works alone.
explanation.definitionFit: A tightly framed shot of a subject is obtained by zooming the camera lens in, which is exactly what this shot needs.

clue.text: Two tools are a puzzle

parts.note: first tool: a jig is a device that guides a cutting tool
second tool: the toothed blade for cutting wood

explanation.surface: Someone is baffled by why a pair of workshop tools amounts to a brainteaser.
explanation.walkthrough: Both pieces come from 'Two tools': name two tools and join them.
explanation.definitionFit: The interlocking-pieces picture game is a common example of a puzzle, named after the fretsaw used to cut it.

clue.text: Jack's fireplace makes a tinkling sound

parts.note: J is the abbreviation for jack in a pack of cards
an ingle is an old word for a hearth or fireplace

explanation.surface: A man called Jack has a hearth that tinkles.
explanation.walkthrough: INGLE (as in inglenook) is a Scots-derived word for a fireside.
explanation.definitionFit: A light ringing of small bells or coins is a standard sense of this word, used as noun or verb.

clue.text: Woman has awful flu, but remains happy

indicators.note: something awful is in a dreadful state, so these letters come out jumbled

parts.note: Joy is a woman's name
the three letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A woman stays cheerful despite a nasty bout of influenza.
explanation.definitionFit: Joyful and happy are synonyms, both meaning full of gladness or delight.

clue.text: Part Scrooge, part devil: both made to economise

indicators.note: only a portion of the following name is used, the rest being dropped

parts.note: the opening three letters of the name
an imp is a small devil, only part of the full fiend

explanation.surface: Dickens's miser is half devil, and both of them are forced to pinch pennies.
explanation.walkthrough: Scrooge, the miser of A Christmas Carol, makes the surface fit the definition nicely.
explanation.definitionFit: To scrimp is to be sparing or frugal with money, a synonym for cutting back and saving.

clue.text: Flexible plant engaged one

indicators.note: to engage is to take on or hold, so the plant word holds the other inside

parts.note: taken as written
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A supple plant got hold of one thing.
explanation.definitionFit: Something pliant bends easily without breaking, so it is a synonym of flexible.

clue.text: Rarely, perhaps, is the Queen seen with those getting up at dawn

indicators.note: perhaps hints that the preceding words are only one possible arrangement of their letters

parts.note: taken as written for rearranging
taken as written, plus an S that no word of the printed clue supplies
ER stands for Elizabeth Regina

explanation.surface: The monarch is seldom spotted in the company of people who rise at sunrise.
explanation.walkthrough: Rarely and is are rearranged, then ER follows; but that makes only ten letters, and the closing S of the plural has no source in the clue, a slip by the setter.
explanation.definitionFit: People who habitually get out of bed very early in the morning are described by this phrase.

clue.text: Symbol announced for an instrument

indicators.note: something announced is spoken out, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: the word for a sign sounds identical to a percussion word

explanation.surface: A sign is proclaimed to stand for a musical instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: This brass plate struck in percussion sections is a musical instrument.

clue.text: Nothing in caustic mixture is used for soundproofing

definitions.note: describes the use, as in acoustic tiles

indicators.note: places one item inside the other
a mixture blends its ingredients, so the letters of the word before it are stirred up

parts.note: taken as written for rearranging
O is a zero

explanation.surface: A corrosive chemical blend is somehow employed to deaden noise.
explanation.definitionFit: Acoustic panels and tiles are materials designed to absorb sound, so the adjective fits things used in soundproofing.

clue.text: Brynner has energy for Christmas!

parts.note: Yul Brynner, star of The King and I
E is the symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A bald Hollywood actor is full of festive energy.
explanation.definitionFit: Yuletide is the old name for the Christmas season, and the short form is a synonym.

clue.text: Thought about drink, a festive cup

parts.note: to mull something over is to ponder it
a common alcoholic drink

explanation.surface: Someone pondered having a drink at a seasonal party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Thought about drink' reads as one idea, but it splits into two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Hot spiced red wine is a traditional Christmas drink, served by the cupful at seasonal gatherings.

clue.text: Baffling show for medieval audiences

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a play full of puzzles, a whodunnit on stage
second meaning: a Bible-story drama staged by guilds in the Middle Ages

explanation.surface: A puzzling performance put on for people in the Middle Ages.
explanation.definitionFit: Medieval religious dramas depicting Bible stories, staged by craft guilds, are known by this name.

clue.text: Aimed to get at red another way

indicators.note: arranging the letters in a different way gives a new word

parts.note: the eight letters of these three words

explanation.surface: Someone tried a different route to reach a red target.
explanation.definitionFit: To have targeted something is to have aimed at it, so the past forms are synonyms.

clue.text: He forgives sailor's new lover

parts.note: AB, able seaman, with the 's

indicators.note: a new version of a word has its letters made over in another order

parts.note: taken as written for rearranging

explanation.surface: A man pardons his sailor partner's latest romance.
explanation.definitionFit: One who absolves sins or blame is a person granting forgiveness, as a priest does.

clue.text: Seed of vegetable and fruit

parts.note: a green vegetable
a nut is botanically a fruit

explanation.surface: A seed from a plant that is both vegetable and fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: The groundnut is the edible seed of a legume plant, eaten roasted or as butter.

clue.text: Homosexual's acceptance of new tie causes merriment

indicators.note: a new form of the word has its letters arranged afresh
accepting something means taking it in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a synonym, the 's being the possessive of the acceptance
the three letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A gay man's delight at receiving a new necktie sparks jollity.
explanation.walkthrough: The older sense of gay, cheerful, also sits behind the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Gaiety means lighthearted cheerfulness and fun, a close synonym of merriment.

clue.text: Perhaps before DSS nothing was a cushy number!

indicators.note: perhaps signals that what follows is just one possible ordering of the letters

parts.note: before and DSS as written, with nothing giving O

explanation.surface: Life was easy before the benefits office existed.
explanation.walkthrough: The DSS was the UK Department of Social Security, which paid out state benefits.
explanation.definitionFit: A situation of comfort and ease is called this idiom, and a cushy number is British slang for an easy job or life.

clue.text: Layout switched to accommodate expenditure

indicators.note: switching things round changes their positions, so the letters are reordered

parts.note: taken as written for rearranging

explanation.surface: A floor plan was changed to fit in the spending.
explanation.definitionFit: An outlay is money laid out or spent on something, a synonym of expenditure.

clue.text: Bustle around, then faint

indicators.note: moving letters around rearranges their order

parts.note: taken as written for rearranging

explanation.surface: Someone rushes about and then collapses unconscious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'faint' looks like the verb for passing out; it is the adjective meaning slight.
explanation.definitionFit: A subtle trace or hint is a faint one, delicate and hard to detect.

clue.text: Initially sudden trail appeared red in the night sky

definitions.note: a phrase standing for the noun, fair because it describes the thing by where it is found, as in 'one in the night sky'

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of each word that follows

parts.note: heads of these three words
the head of this word

explanation.surface: A shooting star suddenly streaked red across the dark.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures a shooting star; the definition is just the closing phrase, describing the answer by where it is seen.
explanation.definitionFit: A glowing celestial body seen at night, some of which shine reddish, such as a red giant.

clue.text: In audition idiot put on warm clothing

indicators.note: an audition is a hearing, so the word is chosen for its sound

parts.note: nit is slang for a fool, and sounds like a word for needlework
to put on clothes is to wear them

explanation.surface: An actor at an audition foolishly dressed in winter woollies.
explanation.walkthrough: A nit (short for nitwit) is a British word for a fool.
explanation.definitionFit: Jumpers, cardigans and scarves made from wool are knitted garments that keep the wearer warm.

clue.text: Lovely females reportedly to go with 5 across

indicators.note: something reported is said aloud, so the spoken form counts

parts.note: the word that follows the tinkling answer at 5 across in the Christmas song title

explanation.surface: Beautiful women are said to go well with a catchy tune.
explanation.walkthrough: The 5 across answer leads into the Christmas carol title Jingle Bells.
explanation.definitionFit: A belle is a beautiful woman, especially the most admired at a gathering, as in belle of the ball.

clue.text: Upset what journalist found to be liquidised

indicators.note: upsetting something knocks it into disorder, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters rearranged
ED is short for editor

explanation.surface: A distressed reporter discovered something had melted away.
explanation.definitionFit: Ice that has thawed has warmed and become liquid, so it has been made fluid.

clue.text: Dwarf who wants to go to bed?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: one of Snow White's seven dwarfs

definitions.text: who wants to go to bed
definitions.meaning: second meaning: describing someone tired and ready for sleep

explanation.walkthrough: The second definition is a description: the adjective for someone who wants their bed.
explanation.definitionFit: One of the seven dwarfs in Disney's Snow White bears this name, and the adjective describes drowsiness.
